extracted.intended_audience: Governor and Council at Fort St. George; British colonial administrators in the Carnatic
extracted.subtask_description: Official instructions & clauses from Commissioners regarding how to investigate, settle, and administer disputed rights and financial claims between the Nabob of Arcot and the Rajah of Tanjore, with directions on fiscal demands, territorial questions, crop shares, and maintenance of hydraulic works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit demands on the Rajah to four lacs
rubrics_metrics.description: We think it impolitic to insist upon any demands upon the Rajah for the expenses of the late war, beyond the sum of four lacs of pagodas annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a demand might tend to interrupt the harmony which should prevail between the Company and the Rajah, and impede the great objects of the general system. Avoid insisting on larger sums in order to preserve good relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Nabob's just claim to arrears
rubrics_metrics.description: It is by no means our intention in any manner to affect the just claim which the Nabob has on the Rajah for the arrears due to him on account of peshcush, for the regular payment of which we became guaranty by the treaty of 1762.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not undermine the Nabob's claim; use every means to convince the Nabob to allow arrears and growing payments to be received by the Company and carried in discharge of his debt to us, and to insure future payment into his hands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring arrears to account promptly, but consider Rajah's resources
rubrics_metrics.description: We direct you to use all proper means to bring these arrears to account as soon as possible, consistently with a due attention to this consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals (e.g., collecting arrears over three years) for consistency with the Rajah's present resources; recover arrears promptly but not at the cost of imprudent demands that would harm local stability or the Rajah's ability to govern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confine formal settlement to matters connected with the 1762 treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: The objects of the treaty of 1762 appear to be restricted ... the only point now in dispute, which appears to us to be so immediately connected with it as to bring it within the strict line of our duty to ascertain and settle according to the terms and stipulations of the treaty, is that respecting Arnee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give priority to points that are directly within the treaty's scope; other disputes may be related but are not strictly for settlement under the treaty's terms unless Parliament's act or broader policy requires it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain full and circumspect knowledge of disputed points
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to obtain a complete knowledge of the facts and circumstances relative to the several points in dispute ... we have with great circumspection examined into all the materials before us on these subjects, and will proceed to state to you the result of our inquiries and deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully examine records, correspondence, consultations, and testimonies before forming decisions; report findings and reasoning to the Commissioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore Arnee jaghire to Tremaul Row's heir unless forfeiture or peace requires delay
rubrics_metrics.description: We therefore direct, that, if the heir of Tremaul Row is not at present in possession of the jaghire, and has not, by any violation of the treaty, or act of disobedience, incurred a forfeiture thereof, he be forthwith restored to the possession of it, according to the terms and stipulations of the treaty of 1762.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restoration might endanger peace and tranquility, suspend execution of the order and promptly transmit the proceedings and full facts and reasons that actuated such conduct for further instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not dispossess Nabob of Hanamantagoody absent satisfactory evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: We observe that the Nabob is now in the actual possession of this fort and district; and we are not warranted, by any document we have seen, to concur with the wishes of the Rajah to dispossess him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require satisfactory documentary evidence of prior Rajah possession in 1762 before ordering dispossession; in absence of such proof, respect Nabob's current possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the 1775–6 government share of the crop as Nabob's where he was de facto sovereign, but limit demands on Rajah
rubrics_metrics.description: We must be of opinion that the government share of the crop of 1776 belonged to the Nabob, as the then reigning sovereign of the kingdom of Tanjore, he being, de facto, in the full and absolute possession of the government thereof; and consequently that the assignments made by him of the government share of the crop were valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although assignments to the Nabob's creditors are valid, do not compel the Rajah to pay supposed long-past balances after such a length of time. The Rajah should be answerable only for the amount collected by his people; the one lac deposited by the Rajah should be applied locally according to principles of justice, or suspended and referred if difficulties arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and ensure upkeep of the Anicut and related works
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anicut is the source of that prosperity ... it is a most stupendous piece of masonry, but, from the very great floods, frequently requiring repairs, which if neglected ... a general injury done to the whole country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the Anicut's central importance to cultivation and prosperity; provide for its repair and maintenance, investigate attempts to prevent or damage repairs, consult prior investigations (e.g., 1764 inquiry and Mr. report) for guidance on responsibilities and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit interference by Company servants in Rajah's internal concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: It was the Company's positive orders, and that any of their servants so interfering would incur their highest displeasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce Company orders that servants must not interfere in the Rajah's domestic government; protect princely dignity from intrusion by civilians or agents and prevent unauthorized impositions on Rajah's correspondence or authority.
